result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and sidewalks on both sides of the street. Traffic is controlled by stop signs, and temporary plastic barriers have been placed in the roadway, likely serving as a makeshift curb extension or construction zone protection.

hazards.name: Temporary roadway barriers
hazards.description: Orange plastic water-filled barriers are placed in the roadway, which may narrow the travel lane unexpectedly for drivers or create a trip hazard if pedestrians step off the curb.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground in the gutter area

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The intersection geometry allows for relatively high-speed right turns from the side street onto the main road.
hazards.location_in_image: Far right corner of the intersection

interventions.title: Permanent Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Replace the temporary plastic barriers with permanent concrete bulb-outs to permanently shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing zebra markings to high-visibility longitudinal bars to increase driver awareness of the crossing zone.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lower-height lighting fixtures specifically directed at the sidewalk and crosswalk areas to improve nighttime visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk in good condition along a residential building. While the walkway is clear of obstructions, there is no physical buffer or vegetation separating pedestrians from the adjacent on-street parking and travel lane.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the roadway, increasing the proximity of pedestrians to moving or parking vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching drivers if they step into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: The silver car parked at the curb.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at nearby intersections to improve visibility and reduce crossing distances.

result.summary: The street features sidewalks on both sides, with a newly constructed wide walkway on the left and an older, partially obstructed walkway on the right. The environment lacks dedicated pedestrian crossing infrastructure or traffic calming measures, and the absence of a buffer between the sidewalk and the two-lane roadway reduces the sense of protection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bags on the left sidewalk and construction barriers on the right sidewalk narrow the usable walking space.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: A long stretch of roadway without marked crossings may lead to unsafe mid-block pedestrian crossings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or furniture zone to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated space for pedestrians to cross.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, newly paved sidewalk along a stone building with a blank frontage. However, safety is compromised by open pits in the walkway and temporary construction barriers that indicate an unfinished or transitioning streetscape.

hazards.name: Open sidewalk pits
hazards.description: Uncovered rectangular cutouts in the sidewalk pavement create significant tripping and fall hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Middle ground, along the edge of the sidewalk

hazards.name: Temporary barriers
hazards.description: Orange plastic water-filled barriers are placed along the curb, potentially narrowing the usable space or indicating unfinished roadway work.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground at the curb line

interventions.title: Tree Pit Completion
interventions.description: Install street trees with permeable grates or fill the pits to eliminate tripping hazards while providing shade.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety along the blank building frontage.

interventions.title: Permanent Curb and Gutter Completion
interventions.description: Finish the roadway paving and remove temporary barriers to provide a clear, predictable edge for pedestrians and drivers.
